({{Literal translation|Association for Movement Games Stuttgart 1893}}), commonly known as '''VfB Stuttgart''' ({{IPA|de|faʊ̯ɛfˈbeː ˈʃtʊtɡaʁt|-|De-VfB Stuttgart.ogg}}), is a German professional [[sports club]] based in [[Stuttgart]], Baden-Württemberg. The club's [[Association football|football]] team is currently part of Germany's first division, the [[Bundesliga]]. VfB Stuttgart has won the [[List of German football champions|national championship]] five times, most recently in 2006–07, the [[DFB-Pokal]] four times and the [[UEFA Intertoto Cup]] a record two times. In the [[all-time Bundesliga table]] the club sits in fourth place. The football team plays its home games at the [[MHPArena]], in the Neckarpark which is located near the [[Cannstatter Wasen]], where the city's [[Cannstatter Volksfest|fall beer festival]] takes place. Second team side [[VfB Stuttgart II]] currently plays in the [[3. Liga]], which is the highest division allowed for a reserve team. The club's junior teams have won the [[Under 19 Bundesliga#Championship winners|national under 19 championships]] a record ten times and the [[Under 17 Bundesliga#Championship winners|national under 17 championships]] seven times. A membership-based club with over 100,000 members,{{cite web |title=Over 100,000 members! |url=https://www.vfb.de/en/vfb/latest/news/club/2024/ueber-100000-dunkelrote/ |date=3 May 2024 |access-date=9 May 2024 |work=vfb.de}} VfB is the largest sports club in [[Baden-Württemberg]] and the eighth-largest football club in Germany. It has departments for [[fistball]], [[field hockey]], [[track and field]], [[table tennis]], and [[referee (association football)|football referees]], all of which compete only at the amateur level. The club also maintains an [[esports]] department and a social department, the ''VfB-Garde''.
